item.title: Fiji needs $300 million to upgrade sporting facilities - Mazey
item.description: Fiji requires an estimated $300 million to upgrade its sporting facilities, according to Fiji Sports Commission Chairman Peter Mazey. He says the country's ageing infrastructure remains one of the biggest challenges facing local sports.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji requires an estimated $300 million to upgrade its sporting facilities, according to Fiji Sports Commission Chairman Peter Mazey.

He says the country's ageing infrastructure remains one of the biggest challenges facing local sports.

Mazey made the comments while responding to concerns raised by Fiji Pearls coach Michelle Parsons about the standard of netball facilities in the country.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Parsons says the difference between the courts in Fiji and Australia became evident during the Fiji Pearls' recent participation in the Spirit Games in Sydney.

She says the players were amazed by the quality of the playing surface in Australia, describing it as vastly superior to what they are accustomed to in Fiji.

Parsons says the court at Vodafone Arena is slippery, making it difficult for players to stop and change direction naturally during matches.

She adds that the poor surface forces players to mechanically adjust their movements, increasing the risk of injury and affecting performance.

Parsons also highlighted that children as young as eight and nine years old in Australia are playing on courts that are of a higher standard than those available to Fiji's national players.

She stressed that Fiji needs significant investment in sporting facilities if athletes are to compete consistently at the highest level.

Mazey acknowledged the concerns, noting that the courts at Vodafone Arena are shared by several sports, making upgrades more complex.

He said infrastructure is a major challenge across all sporting codes and the financial commitment required is substantial.

Mazey says the Sports Commission estimates it needs about $300 million to modernise sporting facilities around the country, comparing the scale of the investment to constructing a new Colonial War Memorial (CWM) Hospital.

He added that, for now, the commission is working with the resources it has while continuing to seek funding for major upgrades.

Meanwhile, Parsons says Fiji also has an opportunity to strengthen its position in international netball if the sport is included in the 2032 Olympic Games.

She noted that greater male participation is one of the requirements being discussed internationally and believes Fiji compares well with many other countries in encouraging men to play the sport.

item.title: Extra Premier League: Rewa thrash Suva 4-0 to build confidence ahead of OFC campaign
item.description: Rewa FC has received a timely boost ahead of their OFC Men's Champions League campaign after recording a convincing 4-0 victory over Suva FC in their Extra Premier League Round 16 match at Churchill Park. The Delta Tigers produced a dominant performance, with goals from Josaia Sela, Asivorosi Rabo, Semi Matalau and Neemish Prasad securing all three points for Rewa.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC has received a timely boost ahead of their OFC Men's Champions League campaign after recording a convincing 4-0 victory over Suva FC in their Extra Premier League Round 16 match at Churchill Park.

The Delta Tigers produced a dominant performance, with goals from Josaia Sela, Asivorosi Rabo, Semi Matalau and Neemish Prasad securing all three points for Rewa.

Rewa’s strong performance will give the defending champions added confidence as they continue their push in the Extra Premier League.

The win comes at an important time for the Delta Tigers as they prepare to begin their OFC Men's Champions League campaign at Churchill Park next Saturday, where they will meet Vanuatu's Galaxy FC at 3pm.

Meanwhile, Navua FC also recorded a big win in Round 16, defeating Tailevu Naitasiri FC 7-2.

The result strengthens Navua’s position on the points table, while Tailevu Naitasiri’s battle to avoid relegation becomes tougher with only two rounds remaining.

Lautoka FC defeated Nadroga FC 3-1 at Churchill Park.

In yesterday's results, Ba FC defeated Labasa FC 2-1, while Nadi FC beat Nasinu FC 3-2.

Labasa Sanatan Tournament: Namara Sanatan eyes title in final against Krishna's Emily Sanatan
item.description: Namara Sanatan will face football star Roy Krishna's Emily Sanatan in the 2026 CK's Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament final after securing a narrow victory over Lajonia Sanatan in today's semi-final. Namara Sanatan defeated Lajonia Sanatan 1-0 in a hard-fought encounter to book their place in the title decider.
item.content:encoded:
Namara Sanatan will face football star Roy Krishna's Emily Sanatan in the 2026 CK's Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament final after securing a narrow victory over Lajonia Sanatan in today's semi-final.

Namara Sanatan defeated Lajonia Sanatan 1-0 in a hard-fought encounter to book their place in the title decider.

Team captain and current Labasa representative Ashneel Raju says his side is expecting another tough match in the final, adding that playing against a team featuring Krishna will be an exciting and thrilling encounter.

He says it will be a challenging contest, but the team is fully prepared and determined to bring the title home.

Emily Sanatan booked their place in the final after defeating Namolink Sanatan 4-0 in the first semi-final, with Krishna returning to the side after serving a one-match suspension.

The final between Namara Sanatan and Emily Sanatan is expected to kick off at 5.30pm.

Auckland-based Fijian Rajat Rai claims Fiji Golf classic crown
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 02/08/2026 Nineteen-year-old Auckland-based Fijian citizen Rajat Rai has won the 2026 Fiji Golf Classic Amateur Tournament at the Denarau Golf & Racquet Club.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 02/08/2026

Nineteen-year-old Auckland-based Fijian citizen Rajat Rai has won the 2026 Fiji Golf Classic Amateur Tournament at the Denarau Golf & Racquet Club.

While receiving his award, Rai acknowledged the support of his parents, saying he would not have achieved this success without them.

He says his proudest moment of the week was embracing his parents in tears after walking off the 18th hole.

The 19-year-old also thanked family, friends and supporters who travelled from overseas to be part of the occasion, saying he is already looking forward to returning next year.

162 people participated in the men's and women's grades with people came from the US, Canada, Australia, and Fiji.

After the 3 days of competition, Ishaan Shah from New Zealand who plays for New Zealand, and Rajat Rai were tied, forcing a 3 hole playoff, which Rai won.

item.title: Springbok women ready for Fijiana challenge
item.description: The South African Women's rugby team is relishing the challenge of taking on the Vodafone Fijiana XV in their two Test match during the August international window. Speaking to fijivillage Sports, team manager Thandiswa Nxomani says the squad has settled in well and completed its first training session, with the players eager for the challenge ahead.
item.content:encoded:
The South African Women's rugby team is relishing the challenge of taking on the Vodafone Fijiana XV in their two Test match during the August international window.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports, team manager Thandiswa Nxomani says the squad has settled in well and completed its first training session, with the players eager for the challenge ahead.

Nxomani says Fiji will be a formidable opponent, especially after the Fijiana's recent appearance in the Super W Grand Final.

He added that South Africa is well aware of the exciting brand of rugby Fiji plays and the challenge of overcoming the hosts on home soil.

He says the tour is also an important opportunity for the Springbok Women to push themselves outside their comfort zone by adapting to different conditions and time zones, which will be valuable preparation ahead of the Rugby World Cup in Australia.

The Springboks Women will face the Vodafone Fijiana this Saturday at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva before the second Test at Churchill Park in Lautoka on 15th August.

item.title: Labasa Sanatan Tournament: Emily Sanatan boosted by Krishna's return for semifinal clash
item.description: Emily Sanatan will receive a major boost for today's 2026 CK's Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament semifinals with the return of football star Roy Krishna. Krishna is back after serving a one-match suspension, having missed yesterday's quarterfinals after receiving two yellow cards earlier in the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
Emily Sanatan will receive a major boost for today's 2026 CK's Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament semifinals with the return of football star Roy Krishna.

Krishna is back after serving a one-match suspension, having missed yesterday's quarterfinals after receiving two yellow cards earlier in the tournament.

Despite the absence of their star striker, Emily Sanatan produced a determined performance to knock out defending champions Nasea Sanatan in a dramatic penalty shootout and book a place in the semifinals.

Emily Sanatan will face Namolink Sanatan in the first semifinal at 9.40am.

The second semifinal will see Lajonia Sanatan take on Namara Sanatan at 10.40am.

A new champion will be crowned this year, with the winners of the semifinals facing off in the 5pm final at Subrail Park for the 2026 CK's Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament title.
